$comment: Language servers of this pack. `config` is the fragment `factory init` merges into the app repo's .factory/config.json (lsp.servers entries, see docs/code-intelligence.md for every field). `optional` holds further fragments to merge by hand. `install` says how to get each server's binary, per OS (`all` = every OS); `factory lsp setup` prints these lines for a server it cannot find. `verified` says whether this file was proven by running the server through the factory or written from the server's documentation.

verified.how: factory lsp check on a scratch solution (hover, definition, references, diagnostics; prepare ran dotnet tool restore and dotnet restore; --owns wrote a solution filter). This is the eShop setup moved out of the engine. Linux and Windows not run.

leased.csharp: yes: Roslyn loads every project of the solution (several GB on a large one). scope.mjs narrows it to the owned projects and their references when lspd starts with --owns.

all: dotnet new tool-manifest   # only when the repository has no dotnet-tools.json (.config/ or the root; .NET 10 writes it at the root)
git add dotnet-tools.json .config/dotnet-tools.json   # whichever exists; the pinned version is part of the repository; `prepare` runs `dotnet tool restore` in every checkout

requires: the .NET SDK the repository builds with, on PATH or in project.toolPaths (~/.dotnet, ~/.dotnet/tools)
notes: scope.options.solution: solution file relative to the repository root. Needed when the root holds more than one .sln/.slnx, or none.
scope.options.restoreSolution: what to `dotnet restore` when the whole solution is opened, for a solution with projects that cannot be restored everywhere (MAUI workloads, ...).
roslyn-proxy.mjs sends Roslyn's solution/open notification, reports the load state (reportsState), asks for pull diagnostics and drops locations in source-generated files.
.razor and .cshtml have no server here: Roslyn's Razor support needs the editor's Razor extension host.
